Who could be next? Yahoo Sports spoke with NFL general managers, salary-cap executives, personnel evaluators and more to take a pulse of the trade deadline landscape. All were granted anonymity due to the competitive implications of the intel. The summary: Expect more moves during the next week. item.title: Raphinha, Yamal power Barca to Champions League win over Villa
item.description: Lamine Yamal and Raphinha got the goals as Barcelona beat Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday (Josep LAGO) Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side's perfect start to the competition. Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace. Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth. Unai Emery's Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca's greater ability in the final third. The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world. "Yes it was (a good win), I want to dedicate this win to the fans, but today I don't want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus -- may he rest in peace," Raphinha told Movistar. "This can happen to anyone, it's very tough... you're going to play a game and the same thing can happen to you... "From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family." Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to. The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute. The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. "Tonight was a huge learning curve for us and I am sure it will stand us in good stead for the future," McGinn told TNT Sports. "Barcelona made the right decisions at the right times and scored really good goals." Yamal's goal was his 14th in the competition across his career, beating Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe's previous record tally of 13 netted as a teenager in the Champions League. Emery, who endured one of the worst nights of his career away at Barca when helming PSG in 2017 during a 6-1 defeat, may have feared the worst. Coby White has returned to the lineup, and Kon Knueppel is close to making his season debut. Charles Lee told reporters on Monday that Knueppel’s return is imminent, even if a specific date remains unclear. “Nothing specific. He’s right behind Coby [White],” Lee stated before their home matchup versus the Detroit Pistons. The coach added that Knueppel’s return is “right around the corner,” according to DaShawn Brown writing on X. The numbers from last year when White, Knueppel, and Miller played together are mind-boggling. When Miles Bridges was kept off the floor with this group, the offensive rating jumped to 147.6. item.title: Lee Westwood Still Unemployed As LIV 2.0 Talks Stall
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Lee Westwood is still without a contract. The 53-year-old English star told The Chipping Forecast podcast that he is currently “unemployed” as the golf world waits for the next big move. He has not signed a deal for the revamped LIV 2.0 tour set to launch in 2027. BBC Sport reports that Westwood said the terms offered to him did not suit his needs. The league is trying to raise $300 million from BC Partners Credit to keep the project alive, but the former world No 1 remains on the sidelines. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund pulled its support last month, and the league filed for bankruptcy protection. Westwood joined LIV in 2022 when the money was flowing freely. He states now that LIV 2.0 has offered him no “anything agreeable” regarding the planned relaunch. Per Sky Sports , the details of the new format still need work before he will consider signing again. The Captaincy He Walked Away From Westwood’s path to this spot started with a choice about the Ryder Cup. He was a top pick to captain Team Europe for the 2023 event in Rome. He spoke with DP World Tour chief Guy Kinnings about the role after Whistling Straits. “It was put to me whether I’d like to be Ryder Cup captain, and I had started discussions with LIV,” Westwood said. He asked if he could still captain the team if he went to the Saudi-backed league. While Kinnings did not refuse, he indicated that the likelihood of such an outcome remained extremely low. Westwood chose the league over the trophy. He told Yahoo Sports that he had no regrets about that choice. “But we make calls in life, you make a choice, and I have no regrets over the choice I made there.” He felt the captaincy wasn’t the be-all and end-all for him. He wanted to be in control of his own game rather than rely on others. That mindset led him to join LIV Golf in 2022, even as it cost him his spot as a future captain. A Long Road Back to the Tour Returning to the DP World Tour is not simple for Westwood. He gave up his membership when he joined LIV. If he wants to play again, he faces a 10-tournament suspension. BBC Sport reports that his return to competition cannot happen before the May tournament in Turkey. His membership is reinstated on November 12. Jon Rahm also left the series recently, citing changes to the team format he did not like. Sergio Garcia and Ian Poulter have also left LIV in recent weeks. Westwood believes the new series could succeed if costs are cut and enough players are recruited. He noted that good things can come from other people’s decisions. “Good things come out of other people’s decisions,” he told Yahoo Sports. He watched Luke Donald take over as captain and lead Team Europe to success.

item.title: PSG fly out of blocks to hit sorry Villarreal for six in Champions League
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain steamrollered Villarreal in a 6-0 Champions League demolition on Tuesday (JOSE JORDAN) Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain scored four times in the first 17 minutes on their way to a 6-0 demolition of Villarreal in Spain in the Champions League on Tuesday, as the French side shrugged off injuries to key players to maintain their perfect record in the competition this season. Joao Neves, Desire Doue, Senny Mayulu and Fabian Ruiz all struck at the Estadio de la Ceramica as PSG set a record for the fastest team to score four times in a match in Europe'e slite club competition. Ruiz added another early in the second half and teenager David Boly completed a comprehensive demolition of the side that finished third in La Liga last season. "I obviously wasn't expecting that but you get matches where you start in that way," PSG's Spanish coach Luis Enrique told broadcaster Canal Plus. "We were impressive throughout and we are really pleased even if it is very difficult for Villarreal -- but it is hard when you play against a team like us that presses constantly." PSG have probably lost star winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for the rest of the campaign after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee in last month's win over Barcelona, while Ousmane Dembele, captain Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes are also missing just now. Despite that, the Ligue 1 leaders made it 10 straight wins in all competitions, including four in the Champions League as they aim to lift the European Cup for a third season running. They are the only team to have maximum points after four matches in this year's Champions League -- Liverpool, Real Madrid and Real Betis all have maximum points from three games before playing on Wednesday -- and Luis Enrique's prolific side have now scored 20 goals on that run. Like all matches in the Champions League on Tuesday, a minute's silence was held prior to kick-off in tribute to Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife player who died following a collision in a Spanish second-division game on Monday. The poignant silence here was also held to remember the victims of last week's deadly train crash in Spain, in which 69 people were killed. - Record home defeat - Neves opened the scoring from close range in the ninth minute, and PSG netted three more goals in under eight minutes following that. Doue swept in as the hosts were punished for calamitous defending, and Villarreal collapsed under the intensity of PSG's pressing as Mayulu made it 3-0. Spain World Cup star Ruiz rounded off the stunning opening salvo, and the same player finished in style for 5-0 early in the second half after latching onto a ball over the top. The 17-year-old full-back Boly came on for Achraf Hakimi and almost immediately got his team's sixth goal -- his first senior strike coming on his Champions League debut. item.title: Liam Lawson Has 83 Points and Still Says ‘I Don’t Really Know What Else to Do’
item.description: Liam Lawson says he doesn’t know what else he can do to keep his Racing Bulls seat after Mexico, as Peter Bayer’s comments spark new rumors. After he was disqualified from F1 Mexico GP qualifying, Racing Bulls ’ Lawson started from the pit lane and finished seventh. He crossed the line ninth, but penalties to Oscar Piastri and Franco Colapinto moved him up. He now has 83 points and is ninth in the F1 drivers’ standings, only 24 behind Isack Hadjar, while he is comfortably ahead by 41 points of Pierre Gasly. Lawson is the best of the rest and should finish like that by the end of the 2026 season. In a normal scenario, that would be enough to seal an F1 seat. He is 45 points ahead of teammate Arvid Lindblad (38). And yet, there is no confirmation of whether the Kiwi will be retained by Racing Bulls in 2027, although PlanetF1 reports that he’s highly likely to stay, with Tsolov potentially taking a reserve role. Lawson Admits He Doesn’t Know What More to Do It is certainly draining and tiring for Lawson. Every race weekend he feels he has done enough, and still, there are no assurances. Talking to the media after Mexico, he showed first signs of being restless. “Yeah, I mean, it’s obviously a massive shame,” he said. “But it’s something that I’m just having to deal with at the moment. I’m obviously trying to do everything I can each time we get in the race car. But yeah, unfortunately, it’s just Formula One. I don’t really know what else to do, so we’ll just go out next week and try again,” summed up Lawson. It was a heavy weekend for Lawson after a clash with Red Bull’s Max Verstappen in FP2, for which he apologized . The stewards gave both of them a one-place grid drop for the next race. item.title: Ohio State football moving forward with Luke Fahey as starting quarterback
item.description: Ohio State coach Ryan Day wasn’t coy about the Buckeyes’ plans at quarterback this week. Day confirmed freshman Luke Fahey will make a second straight start behind center when the Buckeyes host Oregon on Nov. 7. While a loss at USC on Oct. 31 marked Fahey’s starting debut in place of Julian Sayin, who remains sidelined indefinitely with an injury, Day expressed confidence in Fahey moving forward. “I thought you saw him make some plays,” Day said. “He kept playing all the way to the end. I thought his attitude was good on the sideline, even though we couldn't quite get in some of the red zone opportunities. There’s things to build on for sure.” Fahey had been the Buckeyes’ backup quarterback since the start of the season, but held off sophomore Tavien St. Clair as a rare midseason competition unfolded following Sayin’s injury. Day kept their plans to start Fahey against the Trojans under wraps for most of last week. As Day reflected further on Fahey’s first start, he continued to praise the intangibles that were on display at the Los Angeles Coliseum. “He had command of the huddle,” Day said. “He showed some grit out there and toughness.” It followed feedback from teammates. “I go to the players,” Day said, “the offensive line, the wide receivers, and you say, ‘What's it like in there?’ And they were very positive about his approach out there.” Day also pointed to Fahey’s ability to extend plays. He twice scrambled to avoid the rush and gained 17 yards between the runs. Fahey finished 21 of 38 for 260 yards and one touchdown without an interception. “It was not all perfect,” Day said. “There were certainly things that happened operationally that, for a young quarterback, it was a lot on him, and he was working through it. There were some misthrows. But we expected all that to happen.” A majority of the missed throws were on deep balls. Fahey completed only two of 11 passes that traveled at least 20 yards through the air, according to Pro Football Focus. The most noticeable miss was an overthrown pass to wide receiver Devin McCuin in the second quarter. Instead of connecting with McCuin in the end zone for a 43-yard touchdown as he blew past the coverage, the ball sailed out of bounds. Fahey went deep to star receiver Jeremiah Smith three times, but they connected only once for 27 yards. Each of Smith’s previous games with double-digit catches this season against Illinois and Iowa saw him finish with more than 200 receiving yards, but he had just 83 yards with his 10 catches last week. The missed shots left Fahey with an average of 6.8 yards per attempt against the Trojans. item.title: Kuyt: “Everyone Knows How Much Fenerbahce and Liverpool Mean to Me”
item.description: Liverpool’s league phase Champions League tie against Fenerbahce on Wednesday is a chance for the Reds to push to a perfect 4-0 in Europe’s premier cup competition. And it’s a chance to maybe work out a few of their frustrations following Sunday’s referee-assisted 1-0 defeat to Arsenal. It’s also a reunion with a cult legend at the club, with Dirk Kuyt having recently taken over as interim manager following the recent dismissal of İsmail Kartal. Kuyt played 130 games for the Turkish club after the forward joined them from Liverpool in 2012 after six seasons and 285 games in Red, and after moving into management with spells at clubs in Holland and Belgium, he signed on to be Kartal’s assistant at Fenerbahce back in June. Now, he’s coming up against Liverpool. “First of all, it’s a really special achievement to be in the Champions League for the first time in 18 years with Fenerbahce,” Kuyt said today at his pre-match press conference when asked about coming up against the club he played more games for as a player than any other. “That was something really exciting and you always know you’re going to play against exciting teams. But as soon as the draw came up, I was really excited because everyone knows how much Fenerbahce and Liverpool mean to me. From that moment, I knew it was going be a special occasion for me. “But at the stage we are, I’m not important person—it’s the club. The fans deserve much more, they deserve a good performance. We have good players but we need to show up with good energy, with passion, and to play—and then I think it can be a very special night.” Special, though, doesn’t mean he’s hoping for any result other than a win for his side, who currently sit sixth in the Turkish Super Lig—but 31st out of the 36 sides in the Champions League with just two points to show for their opening four league phase matches and their knockout hopes now quickly fading. “Liverpool are an amazing team but so are Fenerbahce,” Kuyt added. “If the fans will show up, too, I think Europe will see how big this club is.”

item.title: Lightning’s Kucherov Crisis About More Than Money
item.description: David Zalubowski/AP The Tampa Bay Lightning have spent the better part of a decade building a championship-caliber roster around Nikita Kucherov. Now, the franchise’s most productive player is questioning whether the organization deserves to keep him. Saturday, he firmly requested a trade following a face-to-face meeting with general manager Julien BriseBois, and his blunt comments Monday indicated the Lightning may have burned the bridge with their reigning Hart Trophy winner. Kucherov’s trade request has largely been framed as a contract dispute, but he insisted money was never the issue. Instead, Kucherov pointed to what he describes as a breakdown in communication and respect between himself and the GM, claiming that the two have spoken only twice in the last four months. However, it should be noted that BriseBois immediately responded to Kucherov’s request with an equally firm public statement that the Lightning would not trade him. For an organization that has built its identity around winning and star players, the current quagmire is significant. If they can reel back the situations, the Lightning may ultimately face a difficult decision over how much to pay Kucherov. But before they can resolve the financial implications of their inaction, they must confront a more immediate question: How did they allow negotiations with their most indispensable player to reach this point? According to Kucherov, 33, the breakdown was not for lack of opportunity. Reports indicated that the Lightning initially offered the winger a four-year extension carrying a $13 million average annual value in July, followed by a six-year offer at a $15 million AAV in September. Neither proposal was enough to secure his commitment, certainly not in light of Leo Carlsson’s $18 million AAV offer sheet from the Philadelphia Flyers, and the gaggle of players whose salaries are now in that range. With Kucherov’s camp reportedly seeking a six-year deal closer to $20 million annually, the financial gap between the two sides is considerable. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. item.title: Cade Cunningham’s 33-Point Surge Turns Hornets Home Game Into A Blowout
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The final score of 124-91 looks like a standard win, but the real story is how the Pistons took control before the third quarter even ended. Cade Cunningham scored a season-high 33 points on Monday night in Charlotte, N.C., yet he did not even play in the fourth quarter, according to CT Insider . This means the Hornets had already lost the game by the time the final period started. The Associated Press noted that in only three quarters, Cunningham hit 13 of 20 shots while contributing five rebounds, five steals, and seven assists. The young Hornets squad posted a 45-16 run in the third quarter. Reporting for Detroit Bad Boys indicated that 14 of Cunningham’s points came in fewer than three and a half minutes of playing time. Taking full responsibility for the team, he stated “We’re playing too well to not blow these guys out.” The Pistons extended their lead to 29 points when Duncan Robinson and Kevin Huerter hit back-to-back threes. The Third Quarter Collapse By the end of the third quarter, the Pistons held a 98-75 lead after starting with an 11-point halftime advantage. The Hornets coach, Charles Lee, decided to empty his bench early because the result was no longer in doubt. Brandon Miller finished with 17 points for Charlotte, while Naz Reid added 13, but it was not enough to stop the surge. Defending against such efficiency proved difficult as the Pistons made 57% of their floor attempts and 48% from deep. With less than five minutes remaining in the second quarter, Dennis Schroder scored a layup to maintain a two-possession lead, yet the Hornets never returned to contention after that. The Pistons made 13 of their first 24 three-point attempts, setting a tone that the Hornets could not match. This performance marks the Pistons’ third straight win, showing a team that is finding its rhythm at the perfect time. Shooting Numbers Tell the Story The Detroit Bad Boys’ shooting stats are shown. At a certain stage of the game, the Pistons were converting more than 60% of their shots from the floor and 50% from three-point range. Duncan Robinson added 24 points behind six 3-pointers, giving the Hornets a hard time on the perimeter. When 1:17 remained in the third quarter, Cunningham headed to the bench, indicating the coach believed the outcome was settled. This decision allowed the starters to rest while the reserves played out the final minutes. Hornets fans in the arena saw the game become a blowout faster than expected.

item.title: Matheus Cunha in tense exchange of words with Michael Carrick after Man United's dramatic win
item.description: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick and Matheus Cunha exchanged words post-game on Tuesday -Credit:Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images Matheus Cunha and Michael Carrick appeared to exchange words following Manchester United's thrilling victory over AS Roma. Cunha was the standout performer for the Reds as two late goals in three minutes secured a 3-2 win against the Italian side in the UEFA Champions League. After the Brazilian netted the winner, he removed his shirt and leapt into the celebrating United supporters, earning himself a yellow card in the process. Shortly afterward, he collected a second yellow and a resulting red for a late challenge on a Roma player. When the final whistle sounded, Cunha moved to join the post-match celebrations, but was promptly intercepted by Carrick. Following their brief exchange, the former Wolverhampton Wanderers forward appeared visibly upset before making his way toward the Old Trafford tunnel, as per the Manchester Evening News . Soccer star Jesús de Miguel tragically dies aged 30 after mid-game collision as tributes paid Goalkeeper involved in tragic Jesús de Miguel collision 'breaks down' after soccer star's death -Credit:Simon Stacpoole/Offside, Offside via Getty Images The reason behind the Brazilian's apparent frustration following his short conversation with the United manager remains unclear. Nevertheless, Cunha made a point of stopping to acknowledge the elated home supporters before disappearing down the tunnel. While the exact nature of the exchange between Carrick and Cunha remains unknown, it is possible the United boss urged the Brazilian to return to the locker room to avoid any additional sanctions. Players dismissed from the field are typically required to remain in the locker room until the match officials have vacated the pitch. Under IFAB Law 12 (Fouls and Misconduct), a red-carded player who enters the field immediately after the final whistle, whether to celebrate with teammates or confront officials, can be classified as an unauthorized pitch entry and misconduct. United were lackluster in the opening 45 minutes and were deservedly trailing 2-0 at the break, after Matías Soulé and Donyell Malen gave the Serie A club a 2-0 advantage.

item.title: “It was right”: Bruno Fernandes acknowledges his error and backs Michael Carrick after special Champions League comeback
item.description: “It was right”: Bruno Fernandes acknowledges his error and backs Michael Carrick after special Champions League comeback Manchester United produced another Champions League comeback for the ages as they came back from two goals down to beat AS Roma 3-2 at Old Trafford on Tuesday. It was the Matheus Cunha show as the Brazilian won the penalty before grabbing a brace to turn the match on its head. The way the players pressed and counter-attacked at times was a callback to the United of old, and Michael Carrick must utilise this blueprint against Aston Villa next to potentially save his job. It was Bruno Fernandes who kickstarted the comeback with his second penalty after he had missed the initial one. Bruno Fernandes kickstarted United’s comeback Thankfully, the referee had spotted an encroachment that allowed the Portuguese superstar another bite at the cherry. The club captain has been under pressure following his outburst against the head coach before he was dropped against Bournemouth. There have been reports of the pair clearing the air , and now the Portugal international must start delivering on the pitch. He spoke to the broadcasters after the match and took responsibility for his poor recent displays and his public criticism, while vowing to keep at it to change the club’s fortunes. Club captain acknowledges his error “It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media. A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened. “The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn’t performing. And that’s fair. Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right. “The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn’t change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club. And it doesn’t change my aim to win every f—king game that I have ahead of me.” Backing for Carrick The attacking midfielder was asked whether the team were trying to save Carrick’s job, and Bruno Fernandes made it clear that everyone needed that result, including the players and the staff. “We don’t need to save anyone’s job.
